Temu Heath Ledger A pretty good summary for this film is “What if Taxi Driver and The Dark Knight had a child and it had 0 personality? Todd Phillips really tries to create a tribute to Scorsese, but as War Dogs fails to do it, so does Joker.  Todd, again is carried into mediocrity by an amazing performance by one of the greats of our generation, who wastes his talent in this. Joaquin Phoenix puts a really good performance, in my opinion not enough to win the Oscar, thats undeniable, but his performance is clearly not enough to make this film any interesting and nowhere near the performance Heath Ledger put for the real Joker. The writing of his character is also pretty pathetic, a character that has always had political/social motivations gets diminished into a depressed maniac that begins a killing spree because his mom lied to him, that is just as disrespectful as it gets. The whole film feels like a bunch of shorts put together in order to create an overall story with no continuity or direction for the most part. In general, I'd say it's an Oscar bait and a film made for spectators that aren't willing to see the deepness in films, those who just want that served in a silver plate for them, leading to it having no actual real meaning and it feeling absolutely empty. The bizarre and bloody scenes feel like they just serve one purpose, camouflaging how mediocre the rest of the film is, I guess thats another attempt to pay tribute to Taxi Driver, but Taxi Driver is fantastic even without these scenes. I really wish the film was better, because I believe Joker is one of the greatest fiction characters ever,who has been mistreated in a lot of films, ruining his potential.

I saw Joker in IMAX on October 3rd for the Thursday night preview. My initial reaction to this movie was not an appropriate level of cringe, but a blatant shame & facepalming for Arthur Fleck. I find no similarity towards. I know people are going to see it differently because Joker is the story of your passed over struggling man. He has to draw more focus for civil service because of a traumatically abusive upbringing. Growing up I did have a strict, disciplined childhood, but that order sharpened me overtime instead of degrading any sense of cognitive development. However, Joker is the story of a man who never quite has the lucidity of a “real world” because of a broken mind coping with the traumatic past of a violent mother. It's abhorrent to figure out his whole life and inspiration to make the big time like “King of Comedy” is nothing more than a farce to keep Arthur going despite the constant maintenance of a bed-ridden mother. Arthur is deeply flawed and that makes it tough for any well-adjusted audience to really sympathize and I mean sympathy in the sense of “this is a character I want to see succeed.” As we see him try to cope with his ongoing inadequacies, he snaps violently at anything he deems deeply inhuman inhabiting the slums of Gotham. My rating for this movie is not a reflection of the story, but really the characterization of the “struggling neurotic male”. We the audience are given an unreliable narrator that makes the world out to be this apathetic society of malevolent individuals as opposed to a series of inner-city mingling bearing the depth of a mentally disturbed trauma victim, Arthur. The saving grave of this whole charade is Fleck's cathartic violence to everyone that was culpable in his downfall.

Le film paraissait beaucoup plus deep quand j'avais 13 ans... On voit que Todd Phillips a essayé de faire un film intelligent mais tous les thèmes sont abordés de manière superficielle. Le film montre un mouvement de révolte populaire mais sans jamais montrer les raisons de leur colère, leur idéologie, les dynamiques entre les classes sociales. Ils se battent contre "le système" sans jamais nous dire quel système sûrement parce que le réalisateur avait peur de faire un film trop politique. La maladie mentale est aussi représentée de manière ultra caricaturale, Joaquim Phoenix en fait trop, il se sent obligé de sortir des phrases ultra dramatiques ("Are you having negative thoughts 🤔? All I have are negative thoughts 😈") + musique triste pour bien nous faire comprendre qu'il va pas bien. Ducoup au lieu d'avoir un film intéressant sur l'intersection entre la pauvreté et les problèmes de santé mentale qui montrerait un vrai mouvement social avec de vrais revendications on a juste un film sur un mec qui se venge des gens qui ont pas été gentils avec lui parce qu'il est trop dark.

我滿喜歡瓦昆•菲尼克斯(Joaquin Phoenix)選擇以一種纖細、敏感的人格特質來詮釋小丑這個角色，也喜歡導演把電影的重心放在到底是什麼樣的社會與生命經驗，才會讓一個破碎之人一步步成為一個瘋狂惡徒。 這部電影看似是在描繪一個邪惡之人的誕生，乍看之下也為小丑最後的種種惡行安排了許多可以在某種程度上同理他的原因，例如精神疾病、童年虐待，以及強烈的階級剝奪感。 但有趣的是，為什麼我們通常不太會因此認為這部電影是在明顯替暴力行為辯護？而有些牽涉到種族或性別議題的電影，卻常常會引起不同立場的群體之間的爭議與論戰呢？ 我自己猜想，或許是因為相較於一些至今仍存在許多不同理解與爭論的社會議題，「殺人是不對的」在現代社會的日常道德判斷中，已經具有相對穩固的共識。 因此，電影即使花了很多篇幅去描繪一個兇手是如何形成的，觀眾仍然會很清楚：理解一個人為什麼變成這樣，並不等於認同、也不等於正當化他所做的事情。 也正因為這個底線幾乎不需要再特別說明，電影才有餘裕把注意力放在人性的複雜面、灰色地帶，以及人與社會之間可能存在的共同困境。 而這也讓我想到，或許其他仍然存在許多價值衝突的社會議題，也不一定只能透過明確的道德立場來呈現。 當然，一部電影選擇表達某種價值主張，或甚至直接挑戰某些既有的社會觀念，絕對沒有問題。電影可以是抗議、揭露、批判，也可以試圖說服觀眾。而且對於某些仍然存在現實不平等的議題，我完全能理解創作者為什麼希望透過作品去挑戰既有的觀念。 而我比較好奇的則是：除了告訴觀眾「什麼是對的」之外，是不是還能進一步往人的生命經驗裡去探索？ 例如那些衝突如何在複雜的現實中進入一個人的生命，以及它可能造成的孤獨、人際關係撕裂、家庭矛盾、經濟與社會壓力，以及對人性基本尊嚴的追求。 我想，我喜愛的其中一種電影，可能是這樣的： 它不只是關注某個社會議題，也不只是替某種立場發聲，而是更進一步描繪一個真實的人，如何在這個充滿矛盾與複雜衝突的世界裡存活。它不急於把人物變成立場的代言人，也不急於給觀眾一個明確的道德標準答案，而是願意把人性的複雜、荒謬與希望，一一溫柔地攤開在我們面前。

"É impressão minha ou o mundo está ficando mais maluco?" Esse filme é simplesmente fantástico. Todd Phillips apresenta uma visão mais humana e profunda de um dos maiores inimigos do Batman. Em vez de mostrar apenas o Coringa como um psicopata que espalha o caos, acompanhamos Arthur Fleck, um homem fragilizado, solitário e constantemente desprezado pela sociedade, até sua transformação no símbolo do caos que conhecemos. Gotham é sombria, suja, violenta e decadente, uma estética que combina perfeitamente com os temas de desigualdade social, abandono e saúde mental abordados pelo filme. Joaquin Phoenix entrega uma atuação impecável, mergulhando completamente na complexidade emocional de Arthur e transitando entre fragilidade e violência. A história também mexe muito com a cabeça, lembrando Taxi Driver, com momentos desconfortáveis e situações que fazem o espectador questionar o que é real. Apesar do ritmo lento e da duração extensa, é uma experiência muito interessante. O roteiro, a cinematografia e a atmosfera são espetaculares, e o filme consegue fazer refletir sobre sanidade, realidade e a forma como a sociedade trata aqueles que são constantemente negligenciados. No fim, Coringa vai muito além de uma simples história de origem: é uma obra complexa, desconfortável e que realmente fica na cabeça depois dos créditos. Nota: 8/10
